title: Label pipeline
subDomain: composing the content of a shipping label

act2.summary: a new section that must be conditional on weight, and positioned differently depending on destination - before the weight line domestically, after everything internationally

solutions.title: Each optional section is a decorator wrapping the one before it
solutions.tradeoff: Adding a section at either end - the start or the end of the chain - is one new decorator class. Act 2 needs a section in the *middle*, between the address and the weight, and a decorator can only wrap what's already built: the base renderer had to be split into two pieces just to open a seam there, and the composition function ends up building two different chains instead of one.

solutions.title: One fixed skeleton, two subclasses for domestic and international
solutions.tradeoff: The two subclasses were already the right shape for 'the same steps, one varies by destination' - but the skeleton itself had no seam before the weight step, so absorbing act 2 means changing the shared base class (a new hook) as well as both subclasses, not just the one that needed the new behaviour.

solutions.title: The sections are a plain array of functions, built at call time
solutions.tradeoff: A stage is just a value, so inserting one conditionally at a specific position is a two-line change to how the array gets built - no new type, no new class, no seam to open. The price was paid in act 1: nothing enforces that every stage in the array agrees on what a shipment needs, the way an interface or a base class would.

reviewFocus: Does the chosen candidate's WALKTHROUGH.md name what would change my mind about the choice, or does it just describe the code?
In the decorator route, was splitting the base renderer into HeaderAddressRenderer and a separate WeightDecorator actually necessary, or could the signature line have been added another way?
In the template-method route, does the new beforeWeight hook change the base class's behaviour for BOTH subclasses, or only the one that needed it?

Is 'a stage is just a value, so its position is just where it sits in an array' a fair reading of why the pipeline route wins here - and would a reader's CHOICE.md, written before act 2, have said the same thing?
Do all three routes - and buildManifestEntry alongside buildLabel - agree, byte for byte, on which sections appear and in what order, for the same shipment?
